messages:
maria: Heads-up — after the safetensors sharding test yesterday we saw big IO burstiness during concurrent model loads. I want to propose a concrete IO-smoothing + fallback policy so Dedicated doesn't blow OOMs or IO saturate shared disks.

alex: +1. can you sketch what you're thinking?

maria: short version: token-bucket style rate limiter per-device + a small global concurrency cap, plus a deterministic fallback ordering for shards: in-memory pref, then mmap, then streaming over http. also prefetch heuristics that prioritize small critical layers (emb, kv) first.

tariq: sounds reasonable. curious about values and backoff strategy — naive rate limit can make cold starts worse.

maria: agreed. propose conservative defaults and exponential backoff for failed reads. rough config: 
```
io: 
  per_device_bytes_per_sec: 300MB
  global_concurrency: 10
  per_request_budget: 32MB
  initial_read_timeout_ms: 100
  backoff: [100ms, 250ms, 500ms, 1s, 2s]
  prefetch: {layers: ["embeddings", "kv_cache"], window_layers: 2}
  fallback_order: ["memory", "mmap", "stream"]
```
These are tunable — main idea is to smooth bursts and let prefetch move critical pieces in first.

olga: +emoji:heart: Can we make the per_device limit adaptive based on device read bandwidth? e.g., query nvme bandwidth from host and set target to 60% of measured.

maria: yes — runtime will probe vendor bandwidth (simple sequential read) and scale per_device_bytes_per_sec = min(configured, measured * 0.6). fallback to configured if probe fails.

kevin: how do we handle checksum/manifest validation without blocking progress? verifying every shard serially adds latency.

maria: do fast header sanity checks inline (magic + size + utf8 name), then start streaming the payload. full checksum verification runs async and marks shard invalid if it fails — then trigger fallback (mmap->stream or re-download). we will keep a short TTL where degraded (unverified) shards are allowed for inference to avoid stalls, but log and metric.

ciara: what about memory pressure ordering? we should prefer loading embeddings+kv to memory and stream large feed-forward weights.

maria: agreed — prefetch prioritizer scores layers by (criticality, size, estimated decode time). small critical layers get higher priority. large dense ff blocks are low priority and can be served via mmap/stream.

alex: implementation notes: make the limiter a shared async primitive in the loader, expose a per-request budget token with try_acquire(size) semantics. Also add a config flag to disable smoothing for latency-sensitive single-tenant Dedicated pools.

tariq: test plan: microbench with 50 concurrent model spins, vary per_device_bytes and global_concurrency, assert 95p tail load time under 3s and no IO queue depth spikes > 1000. also validate fallback triggers.

olga: i'll add runtime bandwidth probe + unit tests for fallback ordering.

kevin: i'll wire the async checksum flow and metrics (checksum_ok, checksum_fail, degraded_shard_in_use).

maria: deploy-bot will simulate a canary with 10% traffic after merge.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: safetensors-io-smoother v1 -> canary (10%) at 2024-05-28T18:30Z. logs: /var/log/deploys/safetensors-io-smoother-canary.log

ciara: small UX request — add an admin endpoint to evict a specific shard and force re-fetch. Helps post-corruption recovery.

maria: good call. action items: @alex add limiter + config, @olga add probe & tests, @kevin checksum async + metrics, @tariq perf harness, @ciara admin-evict endpoint. I'll draft a short RFC section and update the loader README.

alex: i'll send a PR today with the limiter skeleton.

maria: thanks — let's iterate on numbers after perf runs. :rocket:
